Replacing a weak skip with a 3x3 conv gains more than replacing a stronger op.
Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds a large amount of capacity.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is also none disconnects the input from the cell.
Removing the skip shortcut hurts more than removing a weak op.
Deleting a strong conv on the output edge costs more than deleting a weaker op.
Replacing a conv with pooling loses more than replacing a weak op.

raw:
These hypotheses come from general knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 and from the 20 experiments. The experiments are only weak evidence for most of them.

- **Edge 5 -> nor_conv_3x3, parent e4 = none (higher).** In experiment 4 (e4=none) the gain was large. Without edge 4, the 0->3 and 2->3 paths carry more of the load, so a stronger op on edge 5 matters more.
- **Edge 2 -> nor_conv_3x3, parent e2 = skip_connect (higher).** Experiments 11 and 17 replace skip_connect. Experiment 11 gained a lot, 17 less, so this is uncertain. Replacing a weak op with a conv should gain more than replacing a conv or pool.
- **Edge 3 -> nor_conv_3x3, parent e3 = none (higher).** Experiment 13 shows a large gain when an empty direct edge gets a conv. The direct 0->3 connection gives gradient flow and a conv adds capacity.
- **Edge 0 -> none, parent e1 = none (lower).** In experiment 18, e1=none and removing edge 0 was catastrophic. With edge 1 gone too, node 0 is cut off from the rest of the cell, so accuracy drops much more.
- **Edge 3 -> none, parent e3 = skip_connect (lower).** Experiment 10 shows a big drop. Removing the skip loses the main gradient shortcut.
- **Edge 5 -> none, parent e5 = nor_conv_3x3 (lower).** Experiment 16 shows a large loss. Deleting a strong conv on the output edge costs more than deleting a weak op.
- **Edge 4 -> avg_pool_3x3, parent e4 = nor_conv_3x3 (lower).** Experiment 14 shows a big loss. Replacing a conv with a pool costs more than replacing a weak op.
- **Edge 2 -> nor_conv_3x3, parent e2 = none (higher).** Experiment 2 shows gains on all three datasets. Adding a conv where there was none opens a new path, though it is tested only once.
- **Edge 0 -> nor_conv_3x3, parent e0 = none (higher).** Experiment 19 gained on all datasets, especially IN16. Reconnecting the input to the cell restores a path that is very valuable.
- **Edge 1 -> nor_conv_1x1, parent e1 = nor_conv_3x3 (lower).** Experiment 3 shows a big drop. Downgrading a 3x3 conv to a 1x1 conv reduces receptive field and capacity.
